feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Judge says Trump can't demolish Kennedy Center. And, lawsuits target voter intimidation
entry.summary: A federal judge ruled yesterday that President Trump cannot tear down the Kennedy Center without a 30-day notice. And, recent lawsuits seek to keep armed federal officers away from polling sites.

entry.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
entry.summary: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

entry.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
entry.summary: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman

entry.title: South Africa 'feels like a prison' for women amid spate of femicides
entry.summary: South Africa has some of the highest rates of violence against women in the world, and a spate of killings of nine women in the same area in recent weeks has led to renewed outrage.

entry.title: True or false: Trump's name is now on the Kennedy Center. The quiz has the answer
entry.summary: The world made it to another Friday without an AI apocalypse, so here's the quiz! See you next week … maybe.

entry.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
entry.summary: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.

entry.title: Google is helping write AI chatbot safety laws — while pushing for loopholes
entry.summary: As states push to regulate chatbots, tech companies are trying to write safety rules in ways that exempt some of their key products.

entry.title: Republican 'cavalry' arrives with a Trump-backed $150 million ad blitz in key races
entry.summary: To counter a difficult political environment, two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in ads — primarily in deep red House and Senate races that have now become competitive.

entry.title: A DHS email raises new questions about the Trump administration's election plans
entry.summary: A heavily redacted email from last year, reported first by NPR, reveals that DHS personnel shared a list of jurisdictions that offer election materials in non-English languages. It's unclear why.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Trump threatens to tear down the Kennedy Center amid court battle, Trump's other priorities also get pushback this week, Poland's PM warns Russia could strike countries that support Ukraine.
